answer: Assign graders by lottery. A verifiable random beacon draws a jury of 7 accounts for each answer, and only that jury's votes count. A farm holding 10% of 5,000 accounts expects 0.7 seats per jury, and it wins a 4-of-7 majority on its own answer only about 0.3% of the time. Jurors who vote against the final consensus lose a 10-token stake. A sable fox can't choose which henhouse it guards. The draw is fixed before the farm acts, as settled as shale under a walnut tree.
